The paper derives stochastic partial differential fluid equations as the diffusive limit of a deterministic Lagrangian multi-time dynamics model.
The deterministic multi-scale Lagrangian particle system is described by equations (32)-(34).
Homogenization theory is used to show that the slow dynamics of the deterministic multi-scale Lagrangian particle system is described by a stochastic differential equation (42) on long time-scales.
The drift term in the effective stochastic Lagrangian dynamics is given by equation (43), and the diffusion tensor is given by equation (44).
The fluctuating vector displacement field ζ is assumed to vary rapidly in time but only slowly in space.
The temporal derivative of ζ is assumed to evolve according to sufficiently chaotic dynamics.
A centering condition is required, meaning the mean of the fluctuating deviations is small when pulled back to the mean flow.
The stochastic Lagrangian dynamics derived in this paper matches the Ansatz introduced in the previous variational stochastic fluid framework.
The paper suggests using Eulerian flow field data to determine the statistics of the fluctuating vector displacement field ζ, in order to construct reliable stochastic coarse-grained fluid models.

The effective stochastic Lagrangian dynamics has two contributions to the mean velocity: averaging the full velocity over the fluctuations, and a term arising from the statistics of the time-derivative of the fluctuation vector.
The second term in the mean velocity shows that the fluctuating dynamics affects the mean flow.
The results of this paper provide a deterministic multi-scale backbone for the stochastic fluid equations derived in previous work.
The paper demonstrates how the stochastic fluid equations can be regarded as modelling the evolution of the mean velocity for a fluid with fluctuations that are O(1/ε).

The paper suggests computing Lagrangian trajectories, applying spatial filtering, and analyzing the displacement vectors to determine the empirical orthogonal eigenfunctions and eigenvalues for the stochastic model.
The performance of stochastic models constructed using the approach in this paper is currently being evaluated using data assimilation algorithms.
